sources.publisher: Bright Horizons, From Our Blog (a parent's list, no date shown)
sources.quote: Invite all friends to play – excluding kids isn’t nice. ... Help mom and dad with age-appropriate chores. ... If you see someone being or doing something nice, point it out to your child. ... Draw a picture for a relative and send it to him or her in the mail. ... Share a favorite toy with a friend. ... the best way to teach kindness to kids is to model the behavior yourself.
sources.supports: Inviting everyone to play, age-appropriate chores, pointing out kindness when you see it, a drawing for a relative, sharing a toy and modelling kindness. A childcare company blog list for preschoolers, used as general advice for ages 4 to 8.

sources.title: How to Be a Kindness Role Model for Your Kids
sources.publisher: Greater Good Science Center, UC Berkeley (adapted from The Kindness Advantage)
sources.quote: We can inspire our kids to be kinder by talking about and practicing kindness ourselves. ... When you’re watching a movie or TV show with your child, talk about how one of the characters might be feeling and how you would feel in that situation. ... if you or your child loves to draw, turn some of the drawings into cards for people who are in the hospital.
sources.supports: Parents modelling kindness and talking about why they do it, asking how someone else might feel, and turning a child's drawings into cards for others. A university research centre article, used as general advice.

sources.publisher: Bright Horizons, From Our Blog (a parent's list, no date shown)
sources.quote: Invite all friends to play – excluding kids isn’t nice. ... Help mom and dad with age-appropriate chores. ... If you see someone being or doing something nice, point it out to your child. ... Draw a picture for a relative and send it to him or her in the mail. ... Share a favorite toy with a friend. ... the best way to teach kindness to kids is to model the behavior yourself.
sources.supports: Inviting everyone to play, age-appropriate chores, pointing out kindness when you see it, a drawing for a relative, sharing a toy and modelling kindness. A childcare company blog list for preschoolers, used as general advice for ages 4 to 8.

sources.title: How to Be a Kindness Role Model for Your Kids
sources.publisher: Greater Good Science Center, UC Berkeley (adapted from The Kindness Advantage)
sources.quote: We can inspire our kids to be kinder by talking about and practicing kindness ourselves. ... When you’re watching a movie or TV show with your child, talk about how one of the characters might be feeling and how you would feel in that situation. ... if you or your child loves to draw, turn some of the drawings into cards for people who are in the hospital.
sources.supports: Parents modelling kindness and talking about why they do it, asking how someone else might feel, and turning a child's drawings into cards for others. A university research centre article, used as general advice.

sources.quote: Talk about others’ feelings. ... Suggest how children can show empathy. ... Read stories about feelings. ... Developing empathy takes time.

sources.title: Helping Young Kids Cope with Social Anxiety
sources.publisher: Lurie Children's Hospital of Chicago (Pritzker Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Health)
sources.quote: The goal isn’t to push your child into being outgoing—it’s to help them feel safe and supported as they gradually build confidence. ... Talk about what will happen. ... you can take short breaks outside or in the bathroom before returning. ... Stay calm and neutral, and keep expectations realistic. Celebrate small steps, like waving at another child or staying for the whole party without leaving early.
sources.supports: Telling the child in advance what will happen, short breaks and coming back, no pushing, and celebrating small steps. The page is about birthday parties and preschool for shy children, not about the kindergarten circle; applied to a birthday at gan as general advice.

sources.title: Age-by-Age Birthday Party Guide
sources.quote: Singing and circle activities work better than group games for most threes. ... (If your child is shy, however, keep that in mind when making your plan.) ... Five-year-olds know parties are very important and may enjoy the planning even more than the event itself. That's why it's especially important to involve your five-year-old in the entire process.
sources.supports: Singing and circle activities suit young children, a shy child needs a plan that fits, and five-year-olds enjoy being part of the planning. A parenting page about home parties, applied to a birthday at gan as general advice.

sources.title: Keeping Birthday Stress to a Minimum
sources.quote: They can pick their favorite theme, games, friends and food. The child also gets to experience the decision-making process... ... Having an intimate party allows for making each guest feel just as special as the guest of honor
sources.supports: Letting the child choose parts of the celebration, and a small celebration. A parenting page quoting parent educators, applied to a birthday at gan as general advice.

sources.title: Playful Birthday Party Ideas & Tips for Young Children
sources.quote: Remember, big crowds can overwhelm young kids—not to mention the party-throwing parents. ... Keep the party under 90 minutes for toddlers
sources.supports: Big crowds can overwhelm young children, so keep the celebration small and short. Written about birthday parties for young children; applied to a birthday at gan as general advice.

sources.title: How to Help Your Child Develop Empathy
sources.quote: Talk about others’ feelings. ... Suggest how children can show empathy. ... Read stories about feelings. ... Developing empathy takes time.
sources.supports: Talking about how another child feels, suggesting a way to help, and that empathy takes time. The page is written about infants and toddlers; applied to older children as general advice. Reading stories about feelings is the only support for the personalised story, with no promise of a result.
